clue.text: Able to resist soft topping

parts.note: P is piano, the musical abbreviation for soft
a roof is the topping or covering of a building

explanation.surface: Something that withstands a gentle covering, perhaps a cake's icing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Able to resist' is the sense in waterproof or bulletproof, where the word stands alone as a suffix-like adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof as an adjective means impervious, as in shockproof: able to withstand something.

clue.text: The primary element in a code of conduct

definitions.text: The primary element in a code of conduct

parts.words: The primary element in a code of conduct
parts.note: reads as the first item in a rulebook, and describes a fundamental moral rule

explanation.definitionFit: A principle is a fundamental truth or moral rule on which behaviour is based.

clue.text: Start transcribing notes

indicators.note: transcribing music rewrites it in a new form, so the letters of notes are rewritten in another order

explanation.surface: Beginning to write down a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transcribing' signals an anagram of NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, such as an illness.

clue.text: Harry invested in 'Continental country's perfume'

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is put into a firm

parts.note: France is a country on the Continent, mainland Europe
to harry is to harass, and to rag is to tease or torment

explanation.surface: Someone harried into putting money into a French perfume brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' means put inside, the financial sense dressed up as a container signal; the quoted phrase in the printed clue is only the surface's brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant scent, and perfume is a bottled scent.

clue.text: Called outside at one time, being so big-headed

indicators.note: outside says the word for called sits around the phrase for at one time

parts.note: cited means called, as a witness is called to court
once means at one time, formerly

explanation.surface: Someone summoned in the street years ago was arrogant about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal; 'being so' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited people have an inflated opinion of themselves, the same vanity as being big-headed.

clue.text: Overtake — what sauce!

definitions.meaning: to draw level with someone ahead
a tomato sauce, also spelt ketchup

explanation.definitionFit: To catch up is to reach someone in front; catchup is a variant spelling of the tomato condiment ketchup.

clue.text: Speeded up class report

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for speeded is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ran means speeded along
a rate is a class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A report on a class that was rushed through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell or recount events, as in a report.

clue.text: Lugged like corn?

parts.note: looks like carried like a sack of grain, but lugs are ears, so having ears as a corn stalk does

explanation.definitionFit: Corn grows in ears, and a lug is slang for an ear, so having ears is being lugged.

clue.text: A player who finds his work is no laughing matter

definitions.text: A player who finds his work is no laughing matter

parts.words: A player who finds his work is no laughing matter
parts.note: suggests a joyless worker, but means an actor specialising in serious drama

explanation.definitionFit: An actor who plays roles in tragedies, the opposite of comedy, so his performances are not funny.

clue.text: Politician included among the German wets

indicators.note: included among means placed inside another word

parts.note: das is a German word for the
MP is Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A British politician in a group of soft-line Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wets' looks like a noun for feeble politicians (British slang); it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To damp something is to moisten it slightly.

clue.text: Rent isn't a difficulty right now.

indicators.note: difficulty suggests the letters are in a troubled, muddled state and must be sorted

explanation.surface: A tenant relieved that paying the rent is no trouble at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficulty' is the anagram signal: the letters of RENT ISNT A rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a formal, legal-flavoured adverb meaning immediately, at once.

clue.text: Back Moslem leader and prepare to do battle again

parts.note: rear means back, as in the rear of a house

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Moslem

explanation.surface: A call to support a Muslim chief and go back to war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support; it is the noun, the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to supply weapons once more so as to fight again.

clue.text: Many tear all over the, place to. ' provide for others

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, crossword shorthand for many

indicators.note: all over the place says the letters of tear are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of people rush everywhere to look after others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' is the anagram signal; 'Many' gives a Roman numeral, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or services to other people.

clue.text: The man 'to talk to for capital investment

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
to address someone is to talk to them

explanation.surface: Advice on whom to consult about putting money into a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital investment' sounds financial, but capital is the head and investment is clothing (to invest is to dress), so it is something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear clothes the head, and capital is an old word for head, from Latin caput.

clue.text: It's normal to cut the vegetable

parts.note: par means the normal level, as in feeling below par
a snip is a cut with scissors

explanation.surface: A remark that chopping vegetables is routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Slimming success maybe -. but count dire results

indicators.note: results means the letters of count dire produce something new after rearrangement

explanation.surface: A dieter counts calories with grim outcomes but still loses weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'results' signals the anagram of COUNT DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing weight brings a cut in size or pounds, an instance of making something smaller.

clue.text: The movement away from the land

definitions.text: The movement away from the land

parts.words: The movement away from the land
parts.note: reads like rural emigration to towns, but describes the sea receding from the shore

explanation.definitionFit: When the tide ebbs the water flows out, retreating from the coast.

clue.text: The dull exterior is causing concern

indicators.note: exterior says the dull word is on the outside of the other

parts.note: boring means dull
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull outer surface is worrying someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior' puts BORING outside THE: BO + THE + RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothering means troubling or worrying someone.

clue.text: A decorator has to 'call a couple. of trainees in always

indicators.note: in means the call and trainees go inside the word for always

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
to name is to call

indicators.note: a couple of means two copies of the letter

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A painter must keep summoning two apprentices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal and 'a couple of' doubles the learner's letter; E'ER is a poetic form, and 'has to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An enameller decorates surfaces with a glossy vitreous coating.

clue.text: Not coming to any conclusion

parts.note: sounds like an indecisive debate, but literally means having no finish at all

explanation.definitionFit: Something without a finish goes on for ever, never stopping.

clue.text: A painter's jacket

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Stanley Spencer was an English artist; a spencer is also a short waist-length coat.

clue.text: One may feel "X" is in a woman's clutches

indicators.note: a woman clutching something holds it inside her grasp, so one name surrounds the number

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A kiss, written as an X, lands in a woman's hands as a token of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' is the container signal. 'One may feel' looks like the start of a sentence about emotion, but it is the definition: an insect's feeler.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a feeler, the organ an insect uses to sense by touch.

clue.text: Embassy official a sober person hurt

parts.note: TT is teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: A diplomat injured despite being sober.
explanation.definitionFit: An attache is a junior member of an embassy staff.

clue.text: The office-holder is lying

definitions.meaning: someone currently holding a post, such as a sitting MP
an old adjective meaning resting or leaning on something, from Latin incumbere

explanation.definitionFit: The sitting holder of a position has it as a duty resting on them; the word's literal Latin sense is lying upon.

clue.text: This man' is a source of power

parts.note: taken as written
AC is alternating current, a source of electrical power

explanation.surface: Praise of someone as a powerful force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This man' is the definition: a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a male first name, a biblical patriarch.

clue.text: Some woman going shopping for fruit

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman heads out to buy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'shopping for fruit' as the definition, but that cannot stand for the answer; 'fruit' alone is the definition and 'shopping for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a tropical stone fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Jagged Oriental blossom

parts.note: E stands for east, so Oriental
a rose is a blossom

explanation.surface: Describes an eastern flower with spiky edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Erose is a botanical term for a leaf edge that is irregularly notched, as if gnawed.

clue.text: Dramatic music

parts.note: could mean any stirring score, but names the staged musical drama form

explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a drama set to music and sung.

clue.text: A commercial vehicle can accommodate one of the fliers

indicators.note: a vehicle that can accommodate something holds it inside, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a van is a commercial vehicle for goods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A delivery van with room for a single pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of the fliers' reads as a noun phrase, but 'one' gives I and 'of the fliers' is the adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian is the adjective relating to birds, the creatures that fly.

clue.text: Black stuff around the backbone may colour the food

indicators.note: around says the black stuff goes on either side of the backbone

parts.note: coal is black stuff
a chine is a backbone, especially a cut of meat containing it

explanation.surface: Soot on a joint of meat could stain the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal. The definition describes what the answer does rather than naming it: a substance that may colour food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a red dye made from insects, used to tint cakes and sweets.

clue.text: The meeting's about over, by the way

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
on means over, as a lid sits on a pot
a course is a way or route

explanation.surface: An aside that the conference is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about over' looks like 'nearly finished', but gives C and ON; 'by' joins them to COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a gathering or crowd of people coming together.

clue.text: Egg-white for a girl's make-up

indicators.note: make-up suggests the letters are composed afresh into a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A beauty tip: egg white as a cosmetic for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics; it is the anagram signal for A GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glair is a size or glaze made from egg white, used in bookbinding and gilding.
